I mentioned once a long time ago during a meal prep post that I like to make breakfast sandwiches for my SO. He usually gets taken out to lunch by clients at work, and I cook dinner, so breakfast is the only meal he'll be tempted to eat a doughnut/muffin (or several) at the office. Making breakfast sandwiches ahead of time is easy and they freeze, defrost, and microwave well.

I am able to make each one for $1.17 - $1.25 depending on if I use 1 or two slices of cheese. I buy the 24 pack of Thomas English Muffins from Costco, breakfast sausage that I form into patties, yellow American cheese slices (because if you're gonna eat pseudo-junkfood breakfast, it might as well be the yummiest it can be), eggs which I fry, and Canadian bacon slices because they're already a perfect circle shape.

The sandwiches are either sausage-egg-cheese or canadian bacon (ham)-egg-cheese. I use two slices of ham on each sandwich and 1 sausage patty.

  1. Form sausage into patties and cook; set aside. Don't clean the sausage fat out of the pan.
  2. Fry eggs and set aside (I fry 4 at a time in my cast iron).
  3. Allow cooked ingredient to cool.
  4. Open all English Muffins (don't cut in half with a knife you barbarian!- use a fork and take advantage of the iconic nooks and crannies)
  5. Wrap in wax paper/parchment, then plastic wrap.
  6. Freeze.

I leave a few defrosting in the fridge at a time, and he just takes them to work to nuke in the office. He likes them a lot so if I'm out of town or away for some reason, he'll heat one up for dinner/lunch on the weekends. I estimate each one has about 500-600 kcal.

He's been laying off the carbs recently, so instead of making breakfast sandwiches, I decided to make sausage-spinach-egg muffins. In a bowl I mixed cooked and chopped breakfast sausage links, chopped and seared baby spinach, diced red onion, seasonings, and 1 cup cooked quinoa. Once all the cooked ingredients were cool, I added 14 eggs and a handful of shredded cheddar cheese, then mixed it all up and scooped it into a buttered mini-loaf muffin pan and cooked them for 28 minutes. The leftover that didn't fit into the muffin pan went into a round Pyrex to cook like a crust-less quiche. I estimate each mini loaf to be about 350-400 kcal and easily less than a dollar a piece to make, but I didn't do the exact math on these. Between the mini loaves and the pyrex there's enough for 2 weeks worth of breakfasts for him, and by then he'll welcome the change for something else. I'm thinking ham-goatcheese-mushroom for the next batch.

Daily Devotional

August 14

20 Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word; 21 That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me. - John 17:20-21 (KJV)

Jesus is praying to the Father for His disciples, and this verse tells us, who are born again, that this prayer is for us also. Jesus not only prayed for us, but He then went to heaven where He makes intercession for us with the Father (Hebrews 7:25). With Jesus interceding for us with the Father, how can we not be redeemed, and forgiven of all our failures. If you are not born again, visit our web site, click on “The Gospel” link, and find out how to be born again, and saved, so you can be in fellowship with Jesus and the Father (John 17:3).

It is wonderful to think of being saved from hell, and to have a personal relationship with God, but it is more than that, as we are now one with Jesus and the Father. This means we have the Godhead living inside us, and we have the power to overcome anything that the devil throws at us, including power over him (James 4:7). If you are born again, and have been baptized as Jesus commanded us to be, in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Ghost (Matthew 28:19), then you have the Holy Ghost living inside you. You will not realize the power of the Holy Ghost, until you acknowledge that He is there, and ask Him to give you the spiritual gifts, so that you can fulfill the commands that Jesus gave us, to do the works that He has done (John 14:12). Thank you Father for giving us the Holy Ghost to enable us to do the miracles that Jesus did.
